overview: The two broad functional roles in a food chain, split by whether an organism makes its own food or eats other organisms for it.
genZNote: Producers: the ones who cook their own meals using sunlight. Consumers: everyone else, eating what's already been made.

aspects.label: Source of Energy/Food
aspects.valueA: Make their own food through photosynthesis (or chemosynthesis).
aspects.valueB: Obtain food by consuming other organisms.

aspects.label: Trophic Level
aspects.valueA: Always occupy the first trophic level.
aspects.valueB: Occupy the second trophic level and beyond (primary, secondary, tertiary consumers).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: All energy in most ecosystems ultimately traces back to producers capturing solar energy — the foundation of the entire food chain.
overlay.memoryTrick: Producers make it. Consumers take it.
overlay.commonMisconception: Decomposers are a separate functional category from consumers in many syllabi — they break down dead organic matter rather than consuming living organisms directly.
